title: Two-factor authentication
purpose: Manage the authenticator app and recovery codes used to protect your account.
summary: Protect your own account with an authenticator app and recovery codes. Your laboratory may require one of your account; it never changes your roles.

tasks.title: Turn on two-factor authentication
steps: Under [[Authenticator App]], select [[Activate]] and follow the setup.

tasks.title: See or save your recovery codes
Replace your recovery codes
steps: Under [[Recovery Codes]], select [[Generate]] and confirm. The old codes stop working.

good_to_know: Your laboratory may require a second factor of your account. Then, after signing in without one, you set it up before anything else.
Viewing codes and the other actions here may ask you to confirm your password or a code first.
Each recovery code works once, as an alternative to an app code.
Security keys and passkeys are not offered.

sections.title: Enabled factors and account boundary
paragraphs: Requires sign-in and shows only your own authenticators. This deployment enables Authenticator App and Recovery Codes. Adding them is optional unless the laboratory's second sign-in factor rule (Security settings) covers your account. Security keys, passkeys and trusted-browser shortcuts are not enabled. MFA does not grant laboratory roles.

items.label: Authenticator App
items.description: Displays whether an app is active. Activate opens QR/secret enrollment; Deactivate opens removal confirmation.

items.label: Recovery Codes
items.description: Displays unused count out of ten when a set exists, or No recovery codes set up. Each is an eight-digit, single-use alternative to an app code.

items.label: View / Download
items.description: Shown when MFA is enabled and unused recovery codes exist. View opens the current unused set; Download retrieves recovery-codes.txt as plain text. Codes may be viewed again in this deployment; show-once is not enabled.

items.label: Generate
items.description: Shown when an authenticator is enabled. Opens confirmation to replace all recovery codes, including unused ones. No generation action appears with no enabled authenticator.

sections.title: Enrollment and sensitive actions
paragraphs: Successful first app activation automatically creates recovery codes if none exist and opens their page. Sensitive MFA actions and code viewing/downloading require recent reauthentication, normally within five minutes. The overview itself does not require a fresh check. An unverified email address does not stop activation: sign-up is closed, so every account is one the laboratory created.

When the laboratory requires a second factor of your account and this session was sent to set one up, this page opens while the rest stays closed, and once the app is active it shows Continue, which goes on to the page you were opening when you signed in. Deactivating the app in such a session sends it back to Set up a second sign-in factor.
